records.title: Pod Git applies the pod component twice and authorises only the root
records.disposition: Native production-route fixture confirms normal pod Git discovery 404, private LDP 401, and anonymous nested-repository Git 200 with decoded private synthetic bytes. A correctly rooted direct-service control also decodes current and historical private content. Correcting the root alone would expose normal history to the same insufficient authority decision. This qualifies SP-ACL-REVIEW-01 rather than reproducing its blanket normal-layout claim.
records.acceptance: Repair selection and whole-history export authority together. Exercise normal and nested repositories, private children, historic versions, permitted and denied callers, Git discovery and object delivery. Verify the feature and policy in actual consumers.

records.title: Git CGI permits known hidden-tip requests despite mirror ref hiding
records.disposition: Direct hidden-tip fetches were repaired in 1a66c2d (unchanged). Mirror publication isolation, migration of pre-release mirror stores and migration of their forks are committed and merged into local solid-pod-rs main 9b6143c (Commit A 30135fec, B1 bcaf9cf6, B2 ff8048b). Not pushed, released or deployed. Native route regressions: the original raw-route held-SHA test (200 before, 404 after) and held-object denial across raw, HTML, JSON, archive and smart-HTTP, plus migration and fork fixtures built so an in-place gc cleanup would fail them; nine gates green on each exact committed tree. Subprocess controls: scratch git controls for lease semantics, receive-pack hardening, clone variants and object reachability. Source tracing: Opus security and code reviews and Codex gpt-6-astra cross-vendor audits each round; last verdicts PARTLY SUPPORTED with named, out-of-model or non-arising residuals. The smart-HTTP denial test is defence in depth only (1a66c2d already refused the request). Commit A introduced a smart-HTTP pass-through for invalid path segments (.fork-*.tmp); B1 fixed it; recorded here, not counted separately. A lost-record legacy store was served with 200 before B1 (pre-existing, closed by B1).
records.acceptance: Claim, for remote attackers: no object present at migration time and held (not reachable from any approved branch or tag) is served by a mirror or a fork. Met on local main: fetch and validation in a private candidate store outside repos/; publication of approved commits only by explicit SHA with per-ref lease and hardened receive-pack; marker and journal reader gate on every serving route; boot-time rebuild of legacy stores and forks with object-level verification. Not met: deployment evidence, MSRV 1.89 build, consumer adoption. Out of model: filesystem writers, multiple instances sharing a plugin directory, recycled process-group ids, a fork owner re-pushing bytes they hold.
open_followups: B3 (availability): operator recourse for stores stuck at the attempt limit, over 512 MiB, or behind an unreadable owner directory (an unreadable owner directory makes every boot incomplete and gates every 64-hex owner).
B3 (durability): ancestor-directory fsync; descendant-process cleanup on timeout; the engine's process-exit versus size-check race.
B3 (availability): overlapping ancestor roots fail a whole fork rebuild and leave it gated.
Deployment evidence and MSRV 1.89 build remain unverified.

records.title: [MEDIUM] git-http-backend stderr and absolute server paths leak to remote client on backend errors
records.disposition: Source confirms raw backend diagnostics are interpolated into error Display and server JSON; exact leaked values and a fresh HTTP failure fixture remain unverified. Normal pod routing limits earlier blanket reachability claims.
records.acceptance: Keep detailed diagnostics in server logs; test a sentinel diagnostic and absolute path through every HTTP adapter and ensure neither reaches the client.

records.title: [BUG] GitResponse::error builds JSON by unescaped string interpolation
records.disposition: Unescaped formatting predates the repair. Search finds no production call to GitResponse::error in this workspace, only its unit test and documentation. This establishes a public helper defect, not the claimed deployed injection path.
records.acceptance: Use the existing JSON serializer and assert round-trip fidelity for quotes, backslashes, control characters and Unicode; trace downstream callers separately.

records.title: [BUG] Substring-based is_write misclassifies reads of repos named like a service, and can auto-init on GET
records.disposition: Substring classification predates the repair; source admits service-like repository names into the write branch. No new auto-init-on-GET runtime fixture was executed. Pod push refusal and Forge namespace checks differ and must be assessed separately.
records.acceptance: Parse exact endpoint and query service names consistently; test service-like repository names, read-only requests and disk state with permitted and denied callers.
